subject: SparkWorks contract redlines — runtime carveout & subprocessor questions
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <contracts@sparkworks.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SparkWorks - DPA redlines (runtime carveout + subprocessors)

Hi Irene,

Attached are our legal team's redlines to the Data Processing Agreement. Two items are blocking our internal approvals and I was hoping to get your team's take before we escalate:

1) Runtime carveout: we need a carveout that allows SparkWorks to restrict runtime data leaving the customer VPC — specifically, we require an option for a "no-telemetry" mode and a maximum retention of 30 days for any transient inference metadata.

2) Subprocessors: your redline lists a handful of analytics/observability subprocessors with vague roles. Our procurement team needs explicit operational scopes and the ability to opt-out of certain telemetry processors for regulated workloads.

I've attached the redlines PDF and highlighted the two clauses. Can Product and Security confirm if Redwood can: (a) implement a runtime toggle for telemetry, and (b) provide an explicit subprocessor matrix + opt-out path? If not, what product/security compromises can we offer to get to agreement?

Thanks — Elena

Attachments:
- sparkworks_redlines.pdf (pdf, 1 page summary + redline)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <contracts@sparkworks.com>
Date: 2028-07-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: SparkWorks - DPA redlines (runtime carveout + subprocessors)

Elena — thanks for the quick turnaround and the highlights. Looping in Security (Olga) and Product (Karthik) to weigh in on technical and risk trade-offs.

Quick context for Olga/Karthik: SparkWorks is asking for two things that commonly show up for regulated customers: a) a "no-telemetry" or minimal telemetry runtime mode and a hard retention cap (30 days) for any inference metadata; b) explicit subprocessor roles and an opt-out mechanism for certain analytics vendors.

Ask: please confirm (1) whether the runtime/no-telemetry mode is supported or feasible in the short term, (2) whether we can produce an exports/subprocessor matrix for a per-customer opt-out, and (3) any security controls or compensating measures (pseudonymization, sync-only telemetry, KMS-bound logs) you'd need before we accept a carveout in the DPA.

Goal: provide a single response to SparkWorks within 3 business days with proposed language and a proposed operational path (e.g., feature flag, support SLA change, or contractual guardrails).

Thanks — Irene

--
Irene Choi
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-19T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: SparkWorks - DPA redlines (runtime carveout + subprocessors)

Irene / Karthik — quick read and security take. High level: we can likely accept a scoped runtime carveout for telemetry but only with explicit technical constraints and monitoring.

Concerns / prerequisites:
- Telemetry definition: we need to define precisely what counts as "inference metadata" vs. operational logs. For our runtime, KV cache and prefix traces can leak context; those must be included in "inference metadata" if SparkWorks intends to restrict them.
- Retention: 30 days retention for telemetry is reasonable if: (a) we disable persistent KV snapshots for that customer; (b) telemetry is pseudonymized on ingest; (c) we log access and provide audit logs.
- Subprocessor opt-out: we can produce an explicit subprocessor matrix (see attached suggestion) but opt-outs are operationally significant. Opting out of critical observability processors may degrade our ability to meet SLA; we need an SLA fallback clause (e.g., higher latency SLO or no guaranteed throughput) if they opt out of certain processors.

Action items I propose:
1) Product to draft a minimal runtime profile: "Minimal Telemetry Mode" (MTM) — what is disabled, what remains, and measurable impact on latency/cost.
2) Security to produce a *subprocessor scope* doc with roles and data categories (I attached a suggested clause).
3) Legal + Sales to include an operational fallback paragraph in the DPA that ties opt-out choices to potential performance tradeoffs.

Attachments referenced: security_clause_suggestion.docx (word doc; suggested contract language & checklist)

Olga

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-21T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: SparkWorks - DPA redlines (runtime carveout + subprocessors)

Thanks — bringing Product detail. TL;DR: we can offer an operational compromise that should be acceptable: a documented Minimal Telemetry Mode (MTM) + an explicit per-customer subprocessor manifest + operational opt-out with measured SLO impacts.

Proposal (what Product can commit to within 10 business days):
1) MTM definition: disable persistent KV snapshots and async analytics hooks; keep only synchronous, anonymized error logs necessary for debugging. MTM will:
   - suppress prefix KV dumps to long-term storage,
   - limit request metadata to a hashed request id and model/route identifiers,
   - set telemetry retention to at most 30 days in production for that customer.

2) Subprocessor manifest: we'll provide a CSV export listing subprocessors, roles (observability, metrics, auth), and whether they see any request-level metadata. We'll add a per-customer opt-out flag in the manifest; opting out of observability processors will flip the customer to MTM automatically and may change throughput SLAs.

3) Operational controls: require KMS-bound keys for any exported metadata and an audit log we can share monthly. We will also require a security attestation before enabling MTM (short questionnaire).

4) Rollout consideration: initial customer-specific MTM will be a manual configuration with support involvement. We can productize it later if demand grows.

If this aligns, legal can accept a guarded clause in the DPA that references this operational playbook and ties opt-outs to SLA changes. Olga — flagged the security doc; once you confirm the wording I will draft the language Product prefers.

Karthik
